project: MBL549E Final Project — Taşkışla Walkability Analysis
title: Taşkışla: Historical plan vs. contemporary function — a walkability inquiry
data_source: Manual extraction from ITU Faculty of Architecture official floor plans (Taşkışla Building, 4 levels)
Polyline geometry traced in Rhinoceros 8 by the author
Door and stair connections manually recorded from plans
Geometric attributes computed via Grasshopper + Python (shapely)
Space syntax metrics computed via NetworkX graph analysis

building.name: Taşkışla
building.function_change: Originally military barracks; ITU Faculty of Architecture since 1943
building.dimensions: 132 × 95 m with a central courtyard of 70 × 40 m

research_question: Does Taşkışla's 1850 plan, designed as military barracks, align with the walkability needs of today's architectural education?
narrative: The building was not designed together with its current academic program — a 19th-century military logic now houses 21st-century design education. This project measures the topological accessibility of each space from the main entrance and asks where today's academic priorities align with — and where they conflict with — the historical plan.
methodology: Stage 01 — Manual data collection: 181 spaces extracted from floor plans
Stage 02 — Rhino + Grasshopper: polyline tracing, geometry, area, centroid
Stage 03 — Python + NetworkX: graph construction, space syntax metrics (integration, connectivity, mean depth, step depth)

student.name: Şeyma Olcay
student.course: MBL549E Special Topics in Architectural Design
